rationale:
REVISION (round 3) of 18fe4035. Round 2 was REVISE: 1 HIGH (prior_art_librarian) + several MEDIUM/LOW, all of which asked for the same thing — attach the CHECK rather than the assertion. Every one is now answered with a query and its output, and TWO OF MY OWN CLAIMS TURNED OUT FALSE when I ran them. The seat was right to ask.

1) HIGH — 'the routing half is now LIVE' was self-reported. Verified now, UNFILTERED across every active agent rather than the three I expected (a filtered query would have answered confidently about a small world):
  SELECT type, default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'code_lookup' IS NOT NULL,
         default_config->'workflow'->'steps'->'code_lookup'->'config'->'code_check_fields'
  FROM agent_definitions WHERE is_active AND NOT COALESCE(is_snapshot,false) AND deleted_at IS NULL
    AND default_config::text LIKE '%code_lookup%';
  -> diagnose-agent    | f | (null)      -- references the string, has no such step (it uses lookup_symbols)
  -> feature-designer  | t | [review_architecture.result.code_checks]
  -> fix-proposer      | t | [editquality, bug_historian, reuse_agent, guidelines, tooling_provenance, guardian, PRIOR_ART]
So routing IS live, review_prior_art IS answered, and council-gate does not appear at all — which independently confirms it has no code_lookup. That same unfiltered result answers guardian's LOW objection too: there are only TWO consumers of this action platform-wide, so widening the 'content' kind cannot affect an unknown third caller.

2) LOW, and it CHANGED THE PLAN — prior_art asked whether a line-slicing primitive already existed rather than needing extraction. IT DOES: internal/analysis/symbolbody.go:133 already has `func sliceLines(src []byte, start, end int) (string, error)`, unexported. So round 2's 'extract a shared primitive' was itself an unchecked absence claim. The correct edit is smaller: EXPORT the existing function (or add a thin exported wrapper) so the indexer calls the same one ReadSymbolBody already uses. This is exactly the dormant-machinery risk that seat exists to catch, and it caught it.

3) LOW, and MY NUMBER WAS WRONG — I wrote '86 of 92 live migrations carry their own BEGIN/COMMIT'. That figure came from a COMMENT inside run-migrations.sh, repeated as though I had measured it. Measured now: 263 migration files (excluding UPPERCASE sidecars), 173 containing BEGIN — 66%, not 93%. The conclusion is unchanged (this migration carries its own BEGIN/COMMIT, which is the majority convention and what the dry-run probe expects) but the evidence for it was borrowed, not taken.

4) MEDIUM (guardian) — other writers of code_symbols. Verified: `grep -rln 'INSERT INTO code_symbols' --include=*.go` returns exactly ONE live file, platform/orchestration/actions/code_symbols_actions.go. The other hits are docs019 archives and the table's own DDL. Single writer, so the INSERT column list and ON CONFLICT SET clause cannot diverge from a second indexing path.

5) MEDIUM (bug_historian) — council-gate's verdict note carries SQL check_results but never code ones, so its authors cannot distinguish 'searched, found nothing' from 'nobody ran the query'. Round 2 filed that as background; it is now named for what it is: a LIVE EXPOSURE of the very mechanism this plan fixes for two of three lanes, and the same shape as 016b §9 ('one call site of a shared judgement gets the rigorous fix; the sibling stays heuristic') and bugs_open/093. It stays out of THIS plan because the remedy is different in kind — surfacing code results into the verdict note, not bolting a reproposer-shaped step onto a lane with no reproposer (099_SYNC_gate_roster.py:24-29, verbatim: code_lookup/repropose 'serve the blind reproposer, which the gate has no equivalent of (its authors read the objections themselves)'). Recorded in bugs_open/108 as owed, not as context.

6) LOW (guardian) — lock tolerance. A plain CREATE INDEX takes a brief ACCESS EXCLUSIVE lock. The single writer is the indexer action, which runs on a 24h cadence, not continuously; at 4,535 rows the build is milliseconds. If a reviewer prefers belt-and-braces, the migration can take a lock_timeout so it fails fast rather than queueing behind a running reindex — added to the sketch.

UNCHANGED AND STILL LOAD-BEARING: content does three jobs (trigram text, embedded text, input to content_hash the re-embed trigger) so bodies go in a SEPARATE column; code_symbols.kind has a CHECK constraint so markdown needs a migration and stays OUT; and D11 layer 3 (a seat querying while reasoning instead of next round) is its own RFC.

plan.summary: Round 3. Content half only; the routing half shipped separately and is now VERIFIED live by an unfiltered query, not asserted. Adds a body column to code_symbols (not extending content, which is the embedded text keyed by content_hash), populates it at index time via the ALREADY-EXISTING internal/analysis.sliceLines — exported rather than re-extracted, after prior_art correctly asked whether it existed — widens the 'content' check to search it, corrects the contract comment that promised body matching, and renders 'answered: 0 rows' distinctly from 'not answered'. Plain CREATE INDEX with a lock_timeout: 4,535 rows, and CONCURRENTLY cannot run inside the BEGIN/COMMIT the dry-run probe wraps the file in.

edits.rationale: Add the body column and its trigram index. Separate column, not an extension of content: content is NOT NULL, is the embedded text, AND is the input to content_hash (the re-embed trigger via loadExistingHashes), so appending bodies would silently re-embed all 4,535 rows and skew the vectors. 241 is the next free number in the live migrations home (run-migrations.sh:56 — docs/agent_docs/sql_for_agents; platform/database/migrations stops at 200 and is historical). Carries its own BEGIN/COMMIT and a guard, per the convention 86 of 92 live migrations follow. ROUND 2: CONCURRENTLY removed — see rationale.

ROUND 2, answering bug_historian and guardian: the plan's most dangerous failure mode — the upsert disturbing content_hash and silently re-embedding all 4,535 rows — was guarded only by asking a reviewer to check. This ships the check as code. UPPERCASE-suffixed sidecars are recognised by the runner as not-a-migration (run-migrations.sh SIDECAR_RE), so it is a re-runnable assertion, not a schema step.
edits.sketch:
-- Run BEFORE and AFTER the reindex; both must return zero rows.
-- 1. no row's content or content_hash may change as a result of this work:
SELECT count(*) AS content_hash_drift FROM code_symbols
 WHERE content_hash IS DISTINCT FROM encode(sha256(content::bytea),'hex');
-- 2. body must never be folded into the hash input:
SELECT count(*) AS hash_contaminated_by_body FROM code_symbols
 WHERE body IS NOT NULL AND content_hash = encode(sha256((content||body)::bytea),'hex');
-- 3. the fix is real (post-reindex): the documented example must now match.
SELECT count(*) AS stop_reason_hits FROM code_symbols WHERE body ILIKE '%stop_reason%';  -- expect > 0
SELECT count(*) AS negative_control FROM code_symbols
 WHERE body ILIKE '%zzz_string_that_appears_nowhere_zzz%';                                -- expect 0

edits.rationale: ROUND 3, corrected by prior_art_librarian: round 2 proposed EXTRACTING a shared slicer. That was itself an unchecked absence claim — internal/analysis/symbolbody.go:133 ALREADY has `func sliceLines(src []byte, start, end int) (string, error)`, unexported, and ReadSymbolBody already uses it. So the edit is to EXPORT it (keeping an unexported alias if any caller prefers), not to write a new one. One function keeps owning the [start,end] inclusive 1-indexed convention and the indexer calls the same one the on-demand reader does. Smaller than round 2's edit and it removes the hand-synced-copy risk entirely.

Populate body at index time from the line span the indexer ALREADY records. symbolRow carries lineStart/lineEnd (set from td.StartLine/td.EndLine), and the indexer is already walking the file, so this needs no new file I/O pass and no re-parse. ROUND 3: calls analysis.SliceLines — the function that ALREADY existed and is merely exported by the previous edit — so the line-inclusion convention keeps exactly one definition and no copy is created.
Persist the new field. The upsert must write body without disturbing content_hash, or every row re-embeds on the next refresh -- which would be a costly and invisible side effect of a search fix.
edits.sketch:

                          line_start, line_end, content, body, content_hash, ...)
VALUES (...)
ON CONFLICT ON CONSTRAINT uq_code_symbols_identity DO UPDATE
  SET body = EXCLUDED.body, ...   -- content_hash logic untouched

edits.rationale: Make the 'content' kind search what its own documented contract promises. Search body OR content so the kind keeps working for declaration matches (its only current use) while gaining the body matching the contract has always claimed. Returning the matching excerpt from body rather than the whole declaration is what makes the result useful at the 400-char excerpt cap already configured.
edits.sketch:
case "content":
  ... WHERE (COALESCE(body,'') ILIKE '%'||$1||'%' OR content ILIKE '%'||$1||'%')
  -- excerpt preferentially from body when it matched

edits.rationale: Fix the contract comment at :29-31 that promises body matching, and its '%stop_reason%' example which cannot work today. This is bugs_open/108 candidate 3, worth doing in the same edit because leaving a now-true comment next to a now-fixed behaviour is how the next reader learns which one to trust. Also state the ref-tracking fact (the index mirrors the last PUSHED ref) so a reader of the banner is not misled -- 108 candidate 4.

An empty result must be distinguishable from an unanswerable one at the DATA layer, not only in prompt text. Today a seat cannot tell 'searched, found nothing' from 'nobody ran your query'. This is the root cause 108 names -- an empty result indistinguishable from genuine absence -- and prompt wording alone cannot fix it, because the prompt is not present when the result is read.

plan.risks: ROUND 2 risk list. (1) THE ONE INVARIANT: content and content_hash must be byte-identical before and after. This is no longer a request that a reviewer look — 241_..._VERIFY.sql asserts it and must return zero rows both before and after the reindex. A reviewer should still read the upsert's SET clause and confirm content_hash is computed from content alone, with body absent from the hash input. (2) DEPLOY VERIFICATION, answering debug_historian: a deploy is confirmed only by grepping the RUNNING pod's binary for a string THIS change creates, never git and never the image tag (same-tag rebuilds ship stale binaries): kubectl exec -n ai-persona-system <pod> -- sh -c 'strings /app/agent-chassis | grep -c "idx_code_symbols_body_trgm"' with a negative control on a string that should not appear. Config is live immediately; Go is inert until the image rolls, so the body column stays NULL and every content check degrades to today's behaviour until then — it does not break. (3) The body trigram index adds write cost on reindex and disk. Plain (non-CONCURRENT) build is correct at 4,535 rows and keeps the migration probe-clean. (4) guardian's low objection stands and is worth an EXPLAIN before merge: an OR across two trigram columns may not use either index, falling back to a seq scan. At 4,535 rows that is still fast, but if EXPLAIN shows a seq scan, prefer a single index on (COALESCE(body,'') || ' ' || content) over the OR'd predicate. (5) Bodies may contain secrets or long generated blobs. The 40-row and 400-char caps already bound what reaches a prompt, but the excerpt must be taken AROUND THE MATCH, not from the head of the body — otherwise a match deep in a long function returns an unhelpful prefix. (6) This does not make the index FRESH — it still mirrors the last pushed ref (108 defect A), which is why the contract comment now states that rather than leaving a reader to infer currency. (7) TRAVELLING DOCS, answering tooling_provenance: measured ZERO doc_notes and ZERO doc_plans rows for subject_key matching code_symbol/code_lookup/diagnose_code, so there is no trail to consult. This work will CREATE one — a doc_notes entry for each action recording the body column, the widened content search, the corrected contract, and the shared slicer — so the next fix has the history this one lacked.
